$comment: Every UI surface a config/integration-manifest.json entry may name, and whether it exists. `built` is mechanical: tools/integration-audit/verify-parity.mjs requires the named component to exist and to render data-surface="<surfaceId>". The manifest's per-entry `reachable` is the claim that a user can actually configure that integration through the surface, and it may only be true where the surface is built. The two are separate because a surface can exist and still not configure everything it lists -- see Settings > Transcription below.

Settings > Providers.note: Stores a key for every one of the seventeen provider and custom-endpoint credential slots the registry declares -- the three enterprise slots are multi-field and configured on Settings > Intelligence > Enterprise instead -- and runs the real connection test. Write-only: no command returns a credential value, so the field replaces or removes and never displays. A stored key is reported as stored, never as connected.

Settings > Transcription.note: Chooses the cloud provider and model for dictation, from the registry. Six of the seven providers can be selected: three over HttpBatch and three through their own client in crates/transcription-core/src/clients.rs. Corti also takes an environment and a tenant here, because the router refuses to guess either. Tinfoil is listed with the reason it is refused -- an unattested request would present as Tinfoil while providing none of what the name means. Keys are stored on Settings > Providers.

Settings > Transcription > Local.note: Offers whisper models only. The sherpa-onnx sidecar now exists (Task 17) and Task 18 measured and implemented its offline CLI contract for the two Parakeet models -- both transcribe correctly, proven by a real test -- but this screen has not been extended to install or select them, so all four non-whisper local-asr entries stay unreachable: the two Parakeet ones because the runtime is proven but has no selector here yet, and the two Nemotron ones for an unrelated reason -- they are streaming models over sherpa's own WebSocket protocol, which nobody has built a client for. apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/dictation.rs's own comment on LocalTargets names the Parakeet wiring as the anticipated next step.

Settings > Intelligence.note: Configures the reasoning provider and model that tidy a dictation, and switches cleanup on. The three enterprise connectors and the local route are listed with the reason they cannot be used, rather than being left out -- so this surface is built while Settings > Intelligence > Enterprise and > Local are not.

Settings > Intelligence > Local.note: Installs and runs the pinned llama.cpp CPU build and any of the registry's GGUF models. Sizes are shown before the install button because the recommended model is 5.9 GB, and the five-minute idle shutdown is stated rather than being a surprise later.

Settings > Intelligence > Enterprise.note: A form per connector on the Intelligence screen. The request signing and body shapes are written and tested against AWS's published SigV4 vectors and recorded fixtures; no live call has been made, and the section says so on screen as well as in PLATFORM_SUPPORT.md.

Integrations > Calendar.note: Google and Microsoft: register your own OAuth client and paste the client ID in on this screen, then connect and sync -- the screen says why there is no embedded client. Apple shows kw_calendar_core::apple::support()'s reason rather than an empty calendar list.

Integrations > CLI.note: Shows the compiled knegiswhisper binary's location (a real check next to this running application and on PATH, never assumed), the discovery file's path, and the discovery file's real permission state as a tagged union with evidence -- ten states, each with its own sentence in discoveryPermissionsLabel, rather than the boolean is_as_expected() would collapse them to. That boolean has been deleted; DiscoveryPermissions::is_confirmed() draws the line at checked versus unchecked, so owner-and-administrators passes (the access list was read back) and inherited-from-profile does not (nothing looked). See docs/BENCH_CHECK.md, 2026-08-26 finding 2.

Integrations > MCP.note: Shows the exact stdio command line for tools/knegiswhisper-mcp (binary path plus empty args) to paste into an MCP client's config, and states plainly that the local API must be running -- the server has no backend of its own. The binary's presence is a real check next to this running application and on PATH, never assumed.

Notes > Upload.note: Audio, video and URL import (Task 11's media.rs, driving the ffmpeg and yt-dlp sidecars already pinned in config/sidecars.json), plus the OpenWhispr database importer (storage::import::from_openwhispr), which existed and was tested since early in the build but had no screen until now. The screen renders the full ImportReport -- what copied, what was dropped per table, and which credentials moved into the OS credential store -- not just a success message, and states plainly that yt-dlp's own fetch is not policed by kw_network_policy.
